checks: Confirm the review window (2026-09-01 to 2026-11-30) and pull all encounters in it: IDT notes, PCP, cardiology, ED visits, urgent care, and hospital admissions or discharges.

Ischemic heart disease (onset 2026-06-30): review chest pain or angina episodes, nitroglycerin spray use and any refills, cardiology follow-up completed or scheduled, and any ED visits for cardiac symptoms. Flag for team discussion without recommending changes.

Antiplatelet and cardiac medications started 2026-07-07 (clopidogrel, metoprolol succinate, simvastatin, nitroglycerin spray): check adherence and refill gaps, dose changes, new side effects reported (bleeding or bruising, dizziness, bradycardia or low BP, fatigue, GI bleeding), and any new interacting medications or OTCs.
Blood pressure and heart rate trend in the window, including any readings below or above parameters documented in the care plan, orthostatic symptoms, and falls.

Falls and injuries: any falls or near-falls, especially given osteoporosis, scoliosis, chronic pain, and new antiplatelet therapy. Check for fracture, head strike, or bleeding after a fall, and whether a fall-risk assessment was done.

Osteoporosis and alendronic acid (started 2026-06-30): confirm adherence and administration instructions were followed, check for GI symptoms or dysphagia, confirm calcium and vitamin D status and dental review status, and check whether a bone density or fracture-risk review is due.

Chronic pain, chronic intractable migraine, and scoliosis: pain scores and trend, migraine frequency and days per month, rescue medication use, functional impact, and any new pain-related prescriptions or prescriber changes.

Substance use history (dependent drug abuse, onset 2018): review any relapse signals, urine drug screen or monitoring results, pharmacy early-refill or prescriber-shopping flags, controlled-substance prescriptions in the window, naloxone availability, and the treatment or recovery program status. Handle sensitively and surface only what is documented.

Mood, cognition, and sleep: depression or anxiety screen results, any PHQ or GAD scores, cognitive screen if due, and any new distress or hopelessness documented, particularly given a new serious cardiac diagnosis.
Weight and nutrition: weight trend against prior values (BMI 30+ on record), appetite changes, and dietary or cardiac-diet counseling status.
ADLs and IADLs: changes in bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, mobility aids, medication management, and driving or transportation, with the source and date of each assessment.
Dental: impacted molars on record (onset 1991), with dental visit history and any oral pain or extraction plans, which matter given alendronate and antiplatelet therapy.
Caregiver and social situation: living situation, caregiver availability and strain, transportation to appointments, and any changes since the last review (enrollment 2024-04-21).
Attendance and engagement: PACE day-center attendance, transport no-shows, missed appointments, and participant or family engagement in the care plan.

Care-plan items due or overdue: IDT reassessment dates, interdisciplinary care-plan goals and their status, pending referrals (cardiology, pain, behavioral health, dental, PT/OT), and outstanding orders or labs (for example lipid panel or renal function after statin and antiplatelet start, if ordered).
Allergies: the record shows none. Confirm this is current with the participant and pharmacy, since none are documented.

Compile a summary of changes since the last review for the IDT meeting, marking each item as new, changed, unchanged, or unable to verify from the chart, and list open questions for clinician decision.
